issues.title: Skip unpartitioned staging for fixed-width group layouts in hash aggregate sink
issues.hypothesis: Most of the q18 subquery aggregate cost is in the sink. I measured `SELECT l_orderkey, sum(l_quantity) FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey LIMIT 1` at about 410 ms. LIMIT 1 finalizes only a few partitions, and the full aggregate takes about 440 ms, so finalize is roughly 30-50 ms. A plain scan of lineitem is about 57 ms. The aggregate scales almost linearly with threads (4 threads 870 ms, 8 threads 455 ms, 16 threads 350 ms), so it is CPU-bound, not limited by memory bandwidth. Allocator flush settings had no effect. In FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:756-757), new groups go to `unpartitioned_data` when radix_bits >= UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD (3) and new_entry_count/partitions <= 4. On q18 that is about 512 new groups per chunk over 128 partitions, which is exactly 4, so every group takes the staging path. Every Abandon(), which happens every ~16K groups because sink capacity is 32768, then does FlushAppendState, Unpin and Repartition into partitioned_data. Repartition uses DESTROY_AFTER_DONE, and its append state is new each time, so each abandon pins and unpins 128 partitions and frees and reallocates the staging blocks. So each of the 15M groups is written twice and copied once in the sink. An earlier run, recorded in the user's auto-memory, got about -5% on q16 by removing staging for heap layouts. For fixed-width rows, a single direct scatter into the partitions should be cheaper than scatter, copy and repartition.
issues.plan: 1) Measure first. Add temporary steady_clock timers, removed before finishing, around the Repartition inside GroupedAggregateHashTable::Abandon (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:129-146) and around the AppendUnified call in FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (around :765). Report what share of sink time they take on `SELECT max(s) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey, sum(l_quantity) s FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey)`. 2) Change: in FindOrCreateGroupsInternal, take the unpartitioned path only when the layout is not all-constant, i.e. add `!layout_ptr->AllConstant()` to the condition at :756. Alternatively, lower the `<= 4` threshold for fixed-width layouts, e.g. to `< 2`; try both and keep the better one. Leave Abandon/AcquirePartitionedData unchanged: they already handle an empty unpartitioned_data. 3) Compare on and off with repeated `dbe-tool sql` runs (at least 5 warm runs each) of the isolated aggregate and of full q18, not only with bench against best.
issues.expected_gain: q18 0-6% (the sink is about 60% of q18 wall time). The step 1 timers tell us whether the staging copy matters at all.
issues.generality: High-cardinality GROUP BYs with fixed-width keys and states that run with many threads (>2) and reach 3+ radix bits: distinct-heavy group-bys, IN-subquery aggregates, and similar. Could get slower: aggregates with very few new groups per chunk spread over many partitions, where scattering into 128 partitions for a handful of rows has more per-partition overhead than the bulk repartition. Heap (VARCHAR) layouts are unchanged.
issues.risk: Low. A one-condition change on a path that already exists (the partitioned path is used whenever new_entry_count/partitions > 4). Correctness is unaffected, because both paths feed the same partitioned_data.

dispatch: Skip unpartitioned staging for fixed-width group layouts in hash aggregate sink
output.memory:
## Memory (planner, q18 specialisation run)

### Workload facts (q18 only visible template; baseline ~610-650 ms hot, 8 threads)
- Plan: IN-subquery `GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity) > X` over all of lineitem (60M rows -> 15M groups -> ~111 after HAVING).
  HASH_GROUP_BY = 4.6-5.0s CPU. Outer part: lineitem scan 0.17s + probe join 0.26s (60M rows vs 111-row build), orders/customer joins ~0.3s each.
- Group key arrives compressed as UINTEGER (compressed materialization), fixed-width. sum_no_overflow(decimal).
- lineitem is clustered on the key (~4 equal keys per run) -> thread-local HTs dedupe almost fully; finalize sees ~6 dups/117K.

### Key measurements (via dbe-tool sql; multiple ;-separated statements in one call work, the first run is cold)
- Isolated subquery agg ~455 ms wall of q18's ~630. Plain lineitem scan ~57 ms.
- R3: `GROUP BY ... LIMIT 1` (sink + only a few partitions finalized) ~410 ms vs full ~440 => the SINK dominates; finalize ~30-50 ms.
- Thread scaling: 4t 870 ms, 8t 455, 16t 350 => CPU-bound, not bandwidth-bound.
- allocator_flush_threshold / bulk_dealloc threshold = 8GB, block_allocator_memory: no effect (page faults/allocator not the cost).
- Cost is per group (~300ns CPU), grows with row width (no-agg 3.17s, count 4.29s, sum 5.43s CPU for 15M groups).
- Without the aggregate column (count(*) over GROUP BY key) ~330 ms vs ~440 with sum.

### Join-filter finding (R3, not worth pursuing)
- Join filter pushdown can't pass through __internal_compress_integral projections (PushdownJoinFilterExpression only does
  colref/cast), so the outer lineitem probe scan gets NO dynamic filter. With compressed_materialization disabled the
  filters (min/max + bloom) reach the scan: rows 60M->173K and join 0.26->0.03s, BUT scan CPU 0.17->0.54s; q18 wall unchanged.
  dynamic_or_filter_threshold=200: no gain. => Directions that push the join filter through the compress projection are low value.

### Codebase facts
- Radix sink: Sink() -> ht.AddChunk (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519) -> FindOrCreateGroupsInternal (:641).
  New groups go to unpartitioned_data (staging) if radix_bits>=3 && new/partitions<=4 (:756); Abandon() (:129) repartitions
  staging into partitioned_data with DESTROY_AFTER_DONE and a fresh append state. Sink capacity 32768 (>2 threads) -> abandon every ~16K groups.
- DecideAdaptation (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424): SkipLookups if HLL unique >95%; ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD 1M rows.
- MaybeRepartition (:479) grows radix bits (3 -> up to 7 = 128 partitions); ExternalRadixBits caps by reservation.
- Source finalize: RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize builds a new HT per partition + Combine.
- The compressed materialization optimizer runs inside statistics propagation (statistics_propagator.cpp:86), before JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN.
- Settings available: perfect_ht_threshold=12, memory_limit 12.2GiB, disabled_optimizers works.
- profile.md plan is truncated; `dbe-tool profile q18.m0` or `sql "EXPLAIN ANALYZE ..."` prints the full plan.
- The Bash tool rejects shell variables and relative-path reads after cd; inline the full SQL text.

### Directions
- R1 E0001 run-collapse: retired (probe count is not the bottleneck). Correct code, wrong target.
- R2 E0002 in-place finalize: retired, +5%. Finalize is NOT the cost (confirmed by the R3 LIMIT-1 measurement).
- R3 dispatched: skip unpartitioned staging for fixed-width layouts (+ timers on Repartition/AppendUnified in the sink).
  If it is noise, the remaining sink costs are AppendUnified scatter + InitializeStates + UpdateStates on random rows + per-chunk
  partition sel building. Next candidates: (a) a persistent append state / keep staging blocks across abandons;
  (b) a larger sink capacity when dedup is already perfect (fewer abandons); (c) a direct-index HA on dense int keys with
  key-range striping (q13 analog in the auto-memory; the key range is ~4x the group count, so watch memory).
- Backlog: instrument repartition copies (filed R2; partly superseded by R3's timers).
